claims.claim: Customer and government concentration are source-addressed execution risks: one customer represented 82% of Q2 2026 revenue and 74% of first-half revenue, while government customers represented 92% of Q2 revenue and 89% of first-half revenue.

This concentration is not evidence of present deterioration by itself, but it makes revenue continuity sensitive to contract phases, renewals, procurement policy and replacement awards; the filing explicitly notes that expiring U.K. government contracts reduced revenue while higher U.S. government revenue more than offset the decline.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration increases sensitivity to a small number of customer/program decisions and government funding/renewal cycles.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid reported growth coexists with unusually concentrated revenue, so aggregate growth alone is insufficient to establish diversified commercial durability.
contradictions.disposition: source-addressed risk for Alpha underwriting; not a Beta blocker

unknowns.unknown: The economics and renewal probability of the largest customer/program are not established by this filing and remain Alpha-owned underwriting inputs.
